proposal.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets more than doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-02). symptoms: CRM dispute ticket volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-02).
Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 are ESTIMATED-read and 1785 are ACTUAL-read (E-05).

Of the 1240 AMI-channel ESTIMATED-dispute accounts, 1184 had a valid AMI read received before cutoff but rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; only 56 had no read received at all (E-12).
Dispute ticket response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d) despite the volume surge, ruling out handling-capacity as the driver (E-01).
causal_chain: AMI firmware v4.2, rolled out June 2026, reports register readings in 0.1 m3 units instead of whole m3 (E-14).
Billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares the raw register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling applied (E-13).

For v4.2 meters the unscaled raw value is numerically about 10x the true m3 reading, so BV-17 misclassifies valid consumption as anomalous and rejects the read as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION even though it was received before cutoff (E-12: 1184/1240).

Per the meter-to-cash process, a rejected read is treated as no accepted read, triggering estimate substitution so the account receives an ESTIMATED bill instead of one based on its actual valid consumption.
Customers on these accounts dispute the resulting estimated bill, driving the dominant share of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-05) within the Aug-Sep surge (E-02).

proposal.summary: SH-CS reported that billing dispute tickets had doubled since August and asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix wrong bills (CL-01). Investigation showed this was not a response-speed problem (CS already within SLA, E-01) but a wrong-bills problem. CRM data confirmed disputes rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep, E-02). An initial problem definition (PD-1@v1) attributing part of the surge to route-completion gaps was invalidated once AMI read-event data (E-12) showed the dispute bucket in question was dominated by AMI accounts whose reads were received but rejected at billing import, not by missing reads. Further evidence traced the mechanism to validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13); AMI firmware v4.2, rolled out June 2026, reports in 0.1 m3 units instead of whole m3 (E-14), so BV-17 misreads valid v4.2 consumption as anomalous and rejects it, forcing estimate substitution for 1184 of the 1240 AMI-channel ESTIMATED-dispute accounts (95.5%, E-12/E-15). The problem definition was revised to PD-1@v2 to reflect this. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no hold items: the root-cause identification and read-only diagnostic work (dispute-volume monitoring, rule-change log query, AMI read-event query) are released, while no protected actions (bill writes, dispatch changes) were taken, consistent with the authority constraints K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH. Fixing BV-17 itself, correcting the 1184 misrejected accounts, and explaining the larger 1785 ACTUAL-read dispute bucket remain outside this release's completed scope.
key_points: The requester's original frame (an AI agent auto-answering and auto-fixing bills) was treated as a hypothesis, not a given problem; it was rejected (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FIX contradicted by E-01).
Dispute surge confirmed via authoritative CRM data: ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 rising to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-02).
Tariff change and AMI pipeline/delivery failure were ruled out as causes (E-04 zero tariff changes; E-12/E-15 show AMI reads were received, not undelivered).

Root mechanism confirmed: billing validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13) lacks unit scaling for AMI firmware v4.2's 0.1 m3 register unit (E-14), causing valid high-but-correct reads to be rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION for 1184 of 1240 AMI-channel ESTIMATED-dispute accounts (E-12, E-15).

Only read-only diagnostic actions (monitor_dispute_volume, query_rule_change_log, query_ami_read_events) are in release scope; no automated bill writes or dispatch changes occurred, per constraints K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.

Remedies to actually correct BV-17, re-bill the 1184 affected accounts, and add a firmware-compatibility check to future rule deployments were identified (SD-2 remedies) but marked not feasible within contest time and remain unfinished.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no items placed on hold; several verification obligations and unknowns remain open and are tracked as known limitations rather than blockers to this release.
limitations_explained: The 1785 disputed bills based on accepted ACTUAL reads (59% of all disputes, E-05) remain unexplained; BV-17 rejection logic does not apply to them, and the related obligation VOB-U-ACTUAL-DISPUTE-MECHANISM is open despite being flagged as required before release.

The actual code fix for BV-17 (firmware-aware unit scaling) and manual correction/re-billing of the 1184 already mis-rejected AMI accounts have not been done; both require ORG-UTIL change management and SH-BILL manual action under K-BILLWRITE, outside this release's scope.

No committed timeline exists for ORG-UTIL to deploy the corrected BV-17 rule to production (VOB-R-4, required before production, status OPEN), so how long the current read-only detection must remain the only mitigation is unknown.

Handoff data quality is unverified: delivery_status and semantic_validity for both H-FIELD-BILL (manual reads) and H-MDMS-BILL (AMI export) are UNKNOWN, limiting confidence in any future ticket-level correlation.
A process improvement to add firmware-compatibility checks to future billing-rule deployments has been identified as a remedy but not implemented.
The DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some review items were deferred and are tracked as open verification obligations rather than fully resolved before this release.
